content.text:
To pay **federal taxes online**, use the official IRS payments page:

**Best option for most individuals:** **IRS Direct Pay** — pay from a checking or savings account for free, with no sign-in required. It can be used for balance due, estimated tax, extensions, amended returns, installment agreements, and many other individual tax payments. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay?utm_source=openai))

**Go to:** IRS “Payments” page → choose **Direct Pay with bank account**. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments?utm_source=openai))

Other options:
- **IRS Online Account** — sign in to view balance/payment history and pay. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/e-file-providers/paying-your-taxes?utm_source=openai))
- **Debit/credit card** — allowed, but third-party processing fees usually apply. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/e-file-providers/paying-your-taxes?utm_source=openai))
- **EFTPS** — mainly for businesses, large payments, or existing EFTPS users; the IRS says individual taxpayers can no longer create new EFTPS accounts. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/payments/eftps-the-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system?utm_source=openai))

Have ready:
- SSN/ITIN
- Filing status and address from a prior return
- Bank routing/account number
- Tax year and payment type, e.g. **2025 Form 1040 balance due** or **2026 Form 1040-ES estimated tax**

Important: Use only **irs.gov** or **eftps.gov** to avoid scams.
